raw_response:
I farm only 3 mu, so I cannot gamble. At my age, I mostly do what has worked on my land, but I still watch what the neighbors do and what the township technician says. For wheat here in Quzhou, if I want steady grain, I still need enough base fertilizer and two topdressings if the stand looks weak. Water costs money from the well, so I will not irrigate too many times, only at the key stages. After wheat harvest, the maize has to go in quickly. That turnaround is always tight, so I will keep the land prep simple, use hybrid maize seed like most people here, and put fertilizer in a few splits. I would rather spend a bit more on enough fertilizer than see the crop go yellow and lose yield, but with such a small household and little land, I also keep the plan practical and not too input-heavy.
